title.en: Homage to the eldest and the youngest, in field and forest, and to the armed warrior

summary: Fifteen yajus of the same shape as the fifth anuvāka: one namaḥ, two names, each followed by ca. Rudra is saluted as the eldest and the youngest, the first-born and the last-born, then as present in places — the world of men, Yama’s realm, the field and the threshing floor, the Vedic verses and their end, forest and thicket — and in sound and its echo, and finally as the armed warrior with a swift army and chariot, armour, helmet and a renowned host. Sāyaṇa reads most names as Rudra present in a thing, in the form of a thing, or worthy of it.

words.context: ‘be’ (astu) is understood: ‘homage [be] to …’

words.meaning: to the eldest; the greatest, the foremost
words.context: Sāyaṇa: greater [than others] in learning, lordship and the like
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’
Sāyaṇa: the small one, without those [excellences]
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

sandhi.rule: -aḥ before a voiced consonant becomes -o (P. 6.1.114)

vyakarana.note: Superlative in -iṣṭha, with jya- as its stem (P. 5.3.61); ‘eldest’ and ‘most excellent’. The dative goes with namaḥ: ‘homage to X’ takes the dative (P. 2.3.16). So does every name in this anuvāka.
Superlative in -iṣṭha on the stem kan- (‘young, small’), the opposite of jyeṣṭha: ‘youngest, least’.
Each yajus of this anuvāka has the shape namaḥ X ca Y ca: one salutation, two names, each followed by ca.

translation.literal: Homage [be] to the eldest and to the youngest.
translation.readable: Homage to the eldest and to the youngest.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa opens the anuvāka by recalling that the fifth gave yajus with namaḥ on one side only («पञ्चमेऽनुवाके कानिचिदन्यतरतोनमस्काराणि यजूंष्युक्तानि») and that the sixth gives more of the same kind, fifteen of them («विद्यमानानि पञ्चदश यजूंष्याह»). He reads the pair as rank rather than age: «विद्यैश्वर्यादिभिरधिको ज्येष्ठः» — the eldest is the one greater in learning, lordship and the like — and «तै रहितोऽल्पः कनिष्ठः», the youngest is the small one, without them.
units.reflection: One salutation covers the greatest and the least; neither is left outside it.

stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

words.meaning: to the later-born, the one born after
words.context: Sāyaṇa: born at the end of the world, as the fire of time and the like, to withdraw it
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

sandhi.rule: visarga before p becomes the upadhmānīya, written ᳶ in the Taittirīya text (P. 8.3.37)
a + a/ā → ā (akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ, P. 6.1.101)

samasa.meaning: born before, first-born (-ja from √jan, ‘to be born’)
born later, born at the later time

vyakarana.note: -ja is the root jan ‘to be born’ as the last member of a compound; m. dat. sg. in -āya.

translation.literal: Homage [be] to the first-born and to the later-born.
translation.readable: Homage to him who is born first and to him who is born later.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa reads the pair as the beginning and the end of the world: the first-born is «जगदादौ हिरण्यगर्भरूपेणोत्पन्नः पूर्वजः», born at the world’s beginning as Hiraṇyagarbha; the later-born is born in the time of the world’s close, to withdraw it, «कालाग्न्यादिरूपेणोत्पन्नोऽपरजः», in the form of the fire of time and the like.

flags.note: Sāyaṇa’s witness reads सहर्तुं in the gloss on aparaja; the sense ‘to withdraw [the world]’ assumes संहर्तुं, which the context requires. The misprint is in the commentary, not the mantra.

words.meaning: to the middlemost, the middle one
words.context: Sāyaṇa: born in the middle time, as gods, animals and the rest

words.meaning: to the one without boldness; the immature
words.context: Sāyaṇa: a child, whose senses have not yet grown
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

sandhi.rule: -aḥ before a voiced consonant becomes -o (P. 6.1.114)
a + a/ā → ā (akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ, P. 6.1.101)

samasa.meaning: gone from boldness: lacking boldness, immature

vyakarana.note: madhya ‘middle’ with the superlative -ma: ‘middlemost’. m. dat. sg.

translation.literal: Homage [be] to the middlemost and to the immature.
translation.readable: Homage to the one in the middle and to the one not yet grown.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa continues the sequence of the last yajus: the middlemost is born in the middle time, between the world’s beginning and its end — «मध्यकाले देवतिर्यगादिरूपेणोत्पन्नो मध्यमः», in the form of gods, animals and the rest. The apagalbha is a child («बालः»), one whose senses have not yet grown (aparūḍhendriya; the witness misprints the word).

flags.note: Sāyaṇa does not analyse apagalbha. Monier-Williams gives apa-galbha, ‘wanting in boldness’ (galbha ‘bold’); the prādi analysis ‘gone from boldness’ given here is the editor’s, not Sāyaṇa’s.

words.meaning: to the hindmost; the one at the hinder part
words.context: Sāyaṇa: present at the hind part (jaghana) of cows and the like, as their calves
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

words.meaning: to the one at the base, at the bottom
words.context: Sāyaṇa: born at the root (budhna) of trees and the like, as their branches
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

sandhi.rule: -aḥ before a voiced consonant becomes -o (P. 6.1.114)

vyakarana.note: From jaghana ‘hind part’ with -ya (the dig-ādi group takes -ya in the sense ‘being there’). ‘Hindmost, last’ in ordinary use; Sāyaṇa keeps the sense of place.

From budhna ‘bottom, base, root’. The Taittirīya text spells the derivative budhniya- (the dictionaries’ budhnya-, ‘being at the base, of the depths’). A taddhita in -ya, ‘being in, belonging to’ (tatra bhavaḥ, P. 4.3.53); not a compound.

translation.literal: Homage [be] to the hindmost and to the one at the base.
translation.readable: Homage to the one at the hind part and to the one at the root.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa derives both names from a place: jaghanya from jaghana, the hind part — «जघने गवादीनां पश्चाद्भागे वत्सादिरूपेण भवो जघन्यः», present at the hind part of cows and the like in the form of the calf — and budhniya from budhna, the root: «वृक्षादीनां मूले शाखादिरूपेणोत्पन्नो», born at the root of trees and the like in the form of branches.

flags.note: Sāyaṇa’s witness prints both budhna and budhniya with घ for ध (बुघ्ने, बुघ्नियः); the quotation above uses only the undamaged part of the gloss.

words.meaning: to the one in Sobha (sense debated)
words.context: Sāyaṇa: sobha is the world of men, which exists with both (ubha) merit and sin; sobhya is the one present in it
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

words.meaning: to the one of the amulet-cord
words.context: Sāyaṇa: pratisara is the protective band worn on the hand at a wedding and the like; pratisarya is the one worthy of it
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

sandhi.rule: visarga before a sibilant becomes that sibilant (doubled sibilant, as the Taittirīya text writes it; P. 8.3.36 allows visarga or the sibilant)

vyakarana.note: A -ya derivative of sobha. Sāyaṇa takes sobha as sa- ‘with’ + ubha ‘both’ (merit and sin). A taddhita in -ya, ‘being in, belonging to’ (tatra bhavaḥ, P. 4.3.53); not a compound.
From pratisara (prati + √sṛ) ‘cord or band worn as an amulet’; -ya in the sense ‘worthy of it’ (Sāyaṇa: tam arhati).

translation.literal: Homage [be] to the one in Sobha and to the one of the amulet-cord.
translation.readable: Homage to him who is in the world of men and to him of the protective cord.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa analyses sobha as the world that exists together with both merit and sin, that is, the world of men («मनुष्यलोकः»), and supports it with a saying of the Ātharvaṇikas: «पुण्येन पुण्यं लोकं जयति पापेन पापमुभाभ्यामेव मनुष्य लोकम्» — by merit one wins a world of merit, by sin a world of sin, by both the world of men. The one present there is «तत्र भवः सोभ्यः». The pratisara is the protective band held on the hand at a wedding and like occasions: «प्रतिसरो विवाहादौ हस्ते धार्यमाणो रक्षा बन्धस्तमर्हतीति प्रतिसर्यः».

flags.note: The sense of sobhya is not settled. Monier-Williams gives ‘being in or belonging to Sobha’ and ‘a particular personification’; Sāyaṇa’s ‘present in the world of men’ rests on his analysis sa + ubha. The witness prints उभाम्यां and सोमो for उभाभ्यां and the sobha the derivation requires; the quotations above avoid those words.

From kṣema ‘rest, security, well-being’ with -ya. The dictionaries give ‘resting, at ease’; Sāyaṇa’s kṣema is liberation.

translation.literal: Homage [be] to the one of Yama and to the one at rest.
translation.readable: Homage to him who is in Yama’s realm and to him who is in security.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa: «यमलोके पापिशिक्षकरूपेणोत्पन्नो याम्यः» — the one born in Yama’s world in the form of the one who disciplines sinners. Kṣema he takes as liberation (mokṣa): «मोक्षस्तमर्हतीति क्षेम्यः», the one worthy of it is kṣemya.

words.meaning: to the one of the fertile field
words.context: Sāyaṇa: urvarā is land rich in every crop; he is worthy of it, in the form of a particular grain
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

words.meaning: to the one of the threshing floor
words.context: Sāyaṇa: khala is the place where grain is separated; he is worthy of it, in the form of the threshing-post and the like
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

sandhi.rule: -aḥ before a vowel other than a becomes -a: the visarga goes to y (P. 8.3.17) and the y is dropped (P. 8.3.19), leaving the hiatus

vyakarana.note: From urvarā ‘fertile land’ with -ya (the final ā drops before it).
From khala ‘threshing floor’ with -ya.

translation.literal: Homage [be] to the one of the fertile field and to the one of the threshing floor.
translation.readable: Homage to him who is in the ploughed field and to him who is on the threshing floor.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa: the urvarā is «उर्वरा सर्वसस्याढ्या भूमिः», land rich in every crop, and Rudra is worthy of it in the form of a particular grain. The khala is the threshing floor, «धान्यविवेचनदेशः», the place where grain is separated, and he is worthy of it in the form of the threshing-post and the like («मेढ्यादि»). Here Sāyaṇa addresses Rudra in the second person (arhasi, ‘you are worthy’).

words.context: Sāyaṇa: the ślokas are the Vedic mantras; he is present in them as what they teach
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

words.meaning: to the one in the avasāna (end, resting-place)
words.context: Sāyaṇa: avasāna is the Vedānta; he is present there as what it teaches
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

sandhi.rule: visarga before a sibilant becomes that sibilant (doubled sibilant, as the Taittirīya text writes it; P. 8.3.36 allows visarga or the sibilant)
a + a/ā → ā (akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ, P. 6.1.101)

vyakarana.note: From śloka ‘call, sound, praise, verse’. A taddhita in -ya, ‘being in, belonging to’ (tatra bhavaḥ, P. 4.3.53); not a compound.
From avasāna (ava + √so) ‘stopping, end, resting-place’. A taddhita in -ya, ‘being in, belonging to’ (tatra bhavaḥ, P. 4.3.53); not a compound.

translation.literal: Homage [be] to the one in the śloka and to the one in the avasāna.
translation.readable: Homage to him who is in the verse and to him who is in its ending.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa: «श्लोका वैदिकमन्त्रास्तत्प्रतिपाद्यत्वेन तत्र भवः श्लोक्यः» — the ślokas are the Vedic mantras, and Rudra is present in them as the one they set forth. The avasāna, the ending, is the Vedānta: «अवसानं वेदान्तस्तत्प्रतिपाद्यत्वेन तत्र भवोऽवसान्यः».

flags.note: Monier-Williams gives ślokya ‘sounding, noisy’ and avasānya ‘belonging to the line of a verse’; Sāyaṇa takes śloka as the Vedic mantras and avasāna as the Vedānta. The translation keeps the plain words; Sāyaṇa’s reading is in the word table and the traditional note.

translation.literal: Homage [be] to the one in the forest and to the one in the thicket.
translation.readable: Homage to him who is in the forest and to him who is in the undergrowth.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa: «वने वृक्षादिरूपेण भवो वन्यः» — present in the forest in the form of trees and the like; «कक्षे लतादिरूपेण भवः कक्ष्यः» — present in the thicket in the form of creepers and the like.

words.meaning: to sound; to what is heard
words.context: Sāyaṇa: śrava is what is heard, sound
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

words.meaning: to the answering sound, the echo
words.context: Sāyaṇa: pratiśrava is the echo (pratidhvani)
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

sandhi.rule: visarga before a sibilant becomes that sibilant (doubled sibilant, as the Taittirīya text writes it; P. 8.3.36 allows visarga or the sibilant)

vyakarana.note: From √śru ‘to hear’ (guṇa śrav- + -a): ‘hearing, sound’. Rudra is named by the thing itself, without a -ya suffix.
prati + śrava: the sound that comes back. The pañcāśat mark [13] follows this yajus; no sandhi crosses it.

translation.literal: Homage [be] to sound and to echo.
translation.readable: Homage to the sound and to its echo.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa: «श्रूयत इति श्रवः शब्दः» — śrava is what is heard, sound; «प्रतिश्रवः प्रतिध्वनिः», pratiśrava is the echo.
units.reflection: The call and its echo are named together, as though the answer belonged to the voice.

words.meaning: to him whose army is swift
words.context: Sāyaṇa: whose army moves quickly
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

words.meaning: to him whose chariot is swift
words.context: Sāyaṇa: whose chariot moves quickly
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

sandhi.rule: -aḥ before a vowel other than a becomes -a: the visarga goes to y (P. 8.3.17) and the y is dropped (P. 8.3.19), leaving the hiatus
a + a/ā → ā (akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ, P. 6.1.101)

vyakarana.note: senā ‘army’ shortens to -sena as the last member of a bahuvrīhi (P. 1.2.48), and after the u of āśu its s is written ṣ and its n ṇ (-ṣeṇa), as Sāyaṇa also writes it.

translation.literal: Homage [be] to the one with a swift army and to the one with a swift chariot.
translation.readable: Homage to him whose army is swift and to him whose chariot is swift.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa: «आशुः शीघ्रं गामिनी सेना यस्यासावाशुषेणः» — he whose army moves quickly — and «आशुः शीघ्रगामी रथो यस्यासावाशुरथः», he whose chariot moves quickly.

flags.note: Monier-Williams gives āśuṣeṇa as ‘having swift arrows’ (senā ‘missile’ in the oldest texts); Sāyaṇa takes senā as ‘army’, matching śrutasena below. The translation follows Sāyaṇa.

words.meaning: to the hero, the valiant one
words.context: Sāyaṇa: steadfast in battle
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

words.gram: pres. act. participle of ava-√bhid (7th class, P.), m. dat. sg.
words.meaning: to the one who splits, who breaks through
words.context: Sāyaṇa: the one who strikes the enemies
stands after each of the two names: ‘to X and to Y’

sandhi.rule: visarga before a sibilant becomes that sibilant (doubled sibilant, as the Taittirīya text writes it; P. 8.3.36 allows visarga or the sibilant)
a + a/ā → ā (akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ, P. 6.1.101)

vyakarana.note: Present participle of ava-√bhid ‘to split, pierce’ (7th class: present stem bhinad- / bhind-, participle bhindat-), dative singular -e. The preverb stays on the participle.

translation.literal: Homage [be] to the hero and to the one who splits [the foe].
translation.readable: Homage to the hero and to the one who breaks through.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa: «शूरो युद्धे धैर्यवान्» — the hero is the one steadfast in battle; «अवभिन्दन्वैरिणां प्रहर्ता» — the one splitting [them] is the striker of enemies.

flags.note: The two witnesses mark this yajus differently: W1 नम॒श्शूरा॑य (anudātta on ma, svarita on rā), W2 नमः॑ शूराय (svarita on maḥ, the visarga kept, no mark on śūrāya). The text follows W1.

varūtha ‘protection, shelter, house; the guard of a chariot’ with the possessive -in.

translation.literal: Homage [be] to the armoured one and to the one with a shelter.
translation.readable: Homage to him who wears armour and to him who has a shelter.

kavaca ‘cuirass, coat of mail’ with the possessive -in.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa: bilma is the head-protector in battle and the one who has it is bilmin — «युद्धे शिरोरक्षकं तदस्यास्तीति बिल्मी»; «कवचः शरीररक्षकः सोऽस्यास्तीति कवची» — the kavaca protects the body, and the one who has it is kavacin.

flags.note: Sāyaṇa’s gloss on bilma begins «बिल्मं विलेपेतं …» in the witness; विलेपेतं is not clear and is not used here. The rare word bilma is otherwise ‘chip, splinter’ (Ṛgveda), with ‘helmet’ given by the commentators (Monier-Williams: ‘having a helmet’, after Mahīdhara).

senā shortens to -sena as the last member of a bahuvrīhi (P. 1.2.48), as in āśuṣeṇa above; here no retroflexion, since a precedes.

translation.literal: Homage [be] to the famous one and to the one whose army is famous.
translation.readable: Homage to him who is renowned and to him whose army is renowned.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa: «श्रुतो वेदेषु प्रसिद्धः» — śruta is the one famous in the Vedas; «श्रुता वेदेषु प्रसिद्धा सेना» — his army is renowned in the Vedas, and so he is śrutasena. With this the sixth anuvāka closes.
